# The close gate never names the one remedy that works for a duplicate close

## Context / Problem

`close_precheck` exempts a bug closed as `duplicate` / `not_a_bug` / `escalated` from the
billable completion verifier when it names a live replacement:
`src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py:232` calls `_has_live_replacement_link`
(`:49-91`), and on True routes to `close_disposition.verdict()` (`:236-238`).

When that predicate returns **False** the branch simply falls through to the ordinary
completion path (`:241` onwards) and the LLM verifier synthesizes "Bug <title> is actually
resolved", which correctly FAILS — a duplicate's defect is not resolved by the duplicate.
But the remediation text then offers only two impossible paths: complete the unfinished
work (it belongs to the canonical ticket), or mark the criterion `[operator-attested]`
(a false attestation). The single action that works — recording the `duplicates` link — is
never mentioned. Observed on bug 9b70: repeated close failures, nearly escalated for a gate
change or a `--force`; the actual fix was `rebar link 9b70 6a81 duplicates`.

## Approach

Add a deterministic, pre-LLM hard fail at the existing fallthrough. When the ticket is a
`bug` and `close_class == "duplicate"` and `_has_live_replacement_link` returned False,
raise `CommandError` naming the missing link and the exact `rebar link <id> <canonical>
duplicates` command, instead of falling through.

Three decisions, each taken deliberately:

1. **Scope the hard fail to `duplicate` only**, not all of
   `_NON_COMPLETION_BUG_CLASSES` (`close_precheck.py:26`). This follows the operator
   decision recorded on this ticket ("APPROVED to hard-fail a `--class duplicate` close").
   It is also the only class with a canonical counterpart: `not_a_bug` asserts there is no
   defect and `escalated` may point outside the tracker, so demanding a `duplicates` link
   from either would be wrong. Those two keep today's fallthrough behaviour exactly.
2. **Require the link's EXISTENCE, not an open target** — the operator's confirmed
   refinement, since closing a duplicate of an already-closed canonical is the common case.
   No code change is needed to honour this: `_is_live_ticket` (`close_precheck.py:29-46`)
   already accepts any resolvable, non-archived, non-deleted ticket and only rejects
   `status in {"archived","deleted"}` — a `closed` canonical already passes. A regression
   test pins that so a future tightening of `_is_live_ticket` cannot silently reintroduce
   an open-target requirement.
3. **Distinguish a dead target from a missing one.** A new helper reads the same reduced
   state and reports whether a `duplicates` dep (or inbound `supersedes` link) was recorded
   at all. Named-but-unresolvable gets "the ticket you named is archived/deleted/unknown —
   re-link to a live canonical"; nothing recorded gets "you named none — run `rebar link
   …`". This is pure reduced-state reading, so it costs no LLM request.

The new helper is added rather than folded into `_has_live_replacement_link` because two
existing tests monkeypatch that predicate by name
(`tests/unit/test_close_disposition_attestation_738a.py:66,101`); keeping its bool
signature intact keeps the disposition attestation (bug 738a) wiring tests meaningful.

The check sits after the `force_close` early return (`:211`) and after the
`bug_close_class_ok` guard (`:218`), so `--force` still bypasses it and an invalid
`--class` still reports its own error first.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/_commands/close_precheck.py` — new `_recorded_replacement_target()` helper and
  the hard-fail branch at the `_has_live_replacement_link` fallthrough. File is 394 LOC;
  the change keeps it well under the 800-LOC cap.
- `tests/unit/test_close_precheck_duplicate_link_c8fd.py` — new unit test module for the
  four cases below.

## Testing

- Happy path: `--class duplicate` on a bug whose `duplicates` link targets an **open**
  ticket still routes to the disposition verdict (no error, no LLM call).
- Operator-confirmed path: same, but the target is **closed** — must also proceed, proving
  the gate requires link existence and not target openness.
- Failure path: `--class duplicate` with **no** link raises `CommandError` whose message
  contains the literal `duplicates` link command and the ticket id, and the completion
  verifier (`rebar.llm.verify_completion`) is **never** called.
- Edge path: `--class duplicate` naming an **archived/unresolvable** target produces the
  distinct dead-target message, not the "you named none" one.
- Unaffected path: `--class not_a_bug`, `--class escalated`, and a non-disposition class
  such as `plan_defect` with no link all fall through to the completion path unchanged.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `_completion_precheck` raises `CommandError` (returncode 1) for a `bug` closed
      `--class duplicate` with no recorded replacement link, and the message contains
      `rebar link`, the word `duplicates`, and the ticket id.
      Verify: `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_close_precheck_duplicate_link_c8fd.py -q`
- [x] The hard fail runs BEFORE any billable LLM call: the test asserts a monkeypatched
      `llm.verify_completion` recorded zero calls on that path.
      Verify: `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_close_precheck_duplicate_link_c8fd.py -q -k llm`
- [x] A `duplicates` link whose target is **closed** still takes the disposition path (link
      existence only; target need not be open).
      Verify: `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_close_precheck_duplicate_link_c8fd.py -q -k closed`
- [x] A `duplicates` link naming an archived/unresolvable target yields a message that
      names the dead target and differs from the no-link message.
      Verify: `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_close_precheck_duplicate_link_c8fd.py -q -k dead`
- [x] `not_a_bug`, `escalated`, and non-disposition classes are unchanged — no new error on
      the no-link path.
      Verify: `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_close_precheck_duplicate_link_c8fd.py -q -k unaffected`
- [x] The existing disposition-attestation suite still passes unchanged.
      Verify: `python -m pytest tests/unit/test_close_disposition_attestation_738a.py -q`
- [x] Repository gates pass.
      Verify: `make lint && make typecheck && python -m pytest tests/unit -q -k close`

## Provenance

Found closing 9b70 (itself a duplicate of 6a81). Cross-referenced there.
